chosen: This question can be solved using the Hardy Weinberg equation. p2 + 2pq + q2 = 1.  p = frequency of dominant (healthy) allele in populationq = frequency of recessive (Tay-Sachs) allele in population p + q = 1 as all alleles must be either dominant or recessive  We are given that the incidence of Tay-Sachs (q2) is 1 in 320,000 = 1/320,000 = 0.000003200320032003200320032003333  q2 = 0.0000032003333333333333333333333333  q = square root of 0.0000032003333333333333333333333333  q = 0.0017889  p = 1 - q = 1 - 0.0017889 = 0.9982111  2pq = frequency of heterozygotes = carrier women = 2 x 0.9982111 x 0.0

P = 1-q Therefore, p = 1 - 1/1600 = 1599/1600 2pq = 2 x 1599/1600 x 1/1600 = 3198/2,560,000 = 0.00125  This gives a population risk.
